routes.description: Establish God through convergent natural-theology inferences from actualized change, intelligible natural order, objective morality, and interpersonal knowledge.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if these features require a transcendent actual source, ordering intellect, and ground of moral obligation properly identifiable as God.

motionBridge.description: Connect the inferred first cause, ordering mind, and moral ground to the God affirmed by Thomistic theism.

centralBridges.description: Show that dependent change and instrumental causal series require a purely actual first source.
Show that reliable natural regularity and intelligibility require an ordering intellect beyond mindless objects.
Show that obligations independent of human opinion require grounding in a divine intellect.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Defend natural theology as legitimate inference from observed effects to an explanatory cause.
Explain how interpersonal knowledge could warrant belief in God beyond scientific testing alone.

routes.description: Withhold belief unless the affirmative defines God and supplies supported inferences that establish divine attributes rather than merely an unexplained cause.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the proposed proofs leave unsupported causal, methodological, moral, or revelatory gaps, making nonbelief the warranted tentative position.

motionBridge.description: Show that the affirmative evidence does not warrant the conclusion that the claimed God exists.

centralBridges.description: Require a defined claim and valid, evidentially supported demonstration from the side asserting God.
Separate any inferred cause or regularity from the divine mind and maximal attributes claimed.
Account for objective moral assessment relative to human well-being without positing divine moral law.
Require adequate detectable disclosure from a capable personal God who wants to be known.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Limit explanatory candidates to causes that have been independently shown to be demonstrable.
Maintain the negative conclusion tentatively and permit revision upon a sound supported demonstration.

sections.title: Burden of proof and warranted belief
sections.rationale: The governing evidential standard determines what the affirmative must establish and when skeptical nonbelief remains warranted.

sections.title: Change, causation, and the first mover
sections.rationale: The causal inference and the identification of its terminus are indispensable steps in the principal Thomistic route to the motion.

sections.title: Natural theology and scientific explanation
sections.rationale: Whether observations can support extranatural explanatory candidates controls the methodological standing of the affirmative natural-theology inferences.

sections.title: Objective morality and divine grounding
sections.rationale: The existence, meaning, and possible grounding of objective moral judgment form an independent affirmative proof and a central secular alternative.

sections.title: Divine hiddenness and interpersonal knowledge
sections.rationale: A personal God's manner of disclosure bears directly on whether private knowledge can answer the demand for publicly adequate evidence.
